text.en:
Every evening Ravi's grandmother told stories from the Ramayana and the Mahabharata. Sometimes she sang a Tamil verse.
"Where did these stories come from?" he asked.
"They are very old," she said. "Our elders carried them from one generation to the next."

Culture means the way of life of a people: language, food, clothes, festivals, art, music and beliefs. It is passed from elders to children.
The Vedas are among the oldest texts in the world. The Rigveda is the oldest Veda. The Upanishads talk about deep ideas. The epics Ramayana and Mahabharata have been told for thousands of years.
Tamil has one of the oldest literatures in India. Sangam literature is about 2000 years old and tells of love, war and daily life.
Buddhism and Jainism began in India about 2500 years ago, taught by the Buddha and Mahavira, who spoke of non-violence and kindness.
Yoga, classical dance and music, crafts and festivals are also part of our cultural roots. We share ideas with other lands through trade and travel.
Culture is our way of life. It passes from elders to children.
The Vedas are among the oldest texts. The Ramayana and Mahabharata are great epics.
Tamil Sangam literature is about two thousand years old.
Buddhism and Jainism teach non-violence and kindness. Yoga, music and dance are also our roots.

problem.en: Name two ways in which culture is passed on from elders to children.

text.en: Elders tell stories and sing songs.
Children learn customs, festivals and food by taking part.
So stories and everyday practice pass culture on.

prompt.en: A friend says old stories are useless today. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Old stories teach values like kindness, honesty and courage.
They connect us to our past and culture.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking old things have no value.

points.en: Culture is a people's way of life.
Vedas, epics, Sangam literature, Buddhism and Jainism are cultural roots.
Culture passes down through stories and practice.
